result:
I fixed 11 rules in `pricebook.py`. After the fixes, a reference check found every one of the 150 rules matches its docstring.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11, 150 | Labelled "whole" but discounted only the units above the threshold | Discount the full amount |
| 96, 128 | Labelled "marginal" but discounted the full amount | Discount only the units above the threshold |
| 12 | The 30,000 won cap only applied when the discount was over 60,000 won | Always apply the cap |
| 20, 56, 70 | The cap was applied to the price before the percentage, not to the discount | Apply the percentage first, then cap the discount |
| 107 | Charged 3% instead of 2% | Changed to 2% |
| 120, 136 | Charged 6% instead of 5% | Changed to 5% |

I also changed rule 101's condition from `qty > 12` to `qty >= 12` to match the docstring. This doesn't change any result, because a marginal discount at exactly 12 units is 0 anyway.

For the check, I built the expected price for each rule from its docstring (type, rate, threshold and cap) and compared it with the actual code. Quantities 0–129, 500, 1,000 and 5,000 were each tried with 8 unit prices from 0 to 999,999.

STATUS: DONE
